general_conventions: B marks are independent marks awarded only when the specific point is seen in the answer.
M marks are method marks; if an M mark is not scored, the A marks that depend on it cannot be scored.
C marks are compensatory method marks: they can be awarded even if the equation/step is not written, provided later correct working shows it was known.
A marks are accuracy/answer marks that depend on an M mark or allow C marks to be scored; A0 in a 'show that' means the given value earns no mark itself.
ECF (error carried forward): a wrong earlier answer used correctly later is not penalised again.
AW = alternative wording accepted; ORA = or reverse argument; '/' separates alternative acceptable answers; words in brackets are not essential; underlined words must be present.
'reject'/'not' = answers not worthy of credit; 'ignore' = irrelevant statements that neither gain nor lose credit; 'allow' = acceptable answers.

Annotations used include BOD (benefit of doubt), CON (contradiction), ECF, L1/L2/L3 (levels), TE (transcription error), POT (power-of-ten error), SF (significant figure error), WP (wrong physics or equation).
Significant figures: if data are given to 2 s.f., answers to 2 or more s.f. are allowed; an answer to fewer than 2 s.f. is penalised once only in the whole paper unless guidance says otherwise.

Level of Response (6-mark, asterisked) questions: examiner first decides the level (L1 1-2, L2 3-4, L3 5-6) from the science content against the descriptor, then the mark within the level from the quality of communication/line of reasoning; indicative points are guidance, not a checklist; 0 for no response worthy of credit.
Alternative correct answers and unexpected approaches must be credited fairly.

questions.context: Distinguish longitudinal and transverse waves.
questions.answer: Transverse: oscillations perpendicular to direction of energy travel; longitudinal: oscillations parallel to it.
marking_points: B1: transverse - oscillations at right angles to direction of travel/energy transfer
B1: longitudinal - oscillations parallel to direction of travel/energy transfer
allow_reject_ignore: Allow 1 mark for a single statement that one type oscillates at right angles and the other parallel
Allow 1 mark for 'transverse waves can be polarised' (ORA)
pitfalls: Saying particles 'move' along the wave rather than oscillate
Omitting the reference direction (direction of travel/energy transfer)

questions.context: Read amplitude of an oscilloscope trace using the y-sensitivity setting.
pitfalls: Using peak-to-peak height instead of amplitude

questions.context: Find the signal frequency from the trace using the time-base.
marking_points: C1: period T = 3 div × 0.5 ms = 1.5 ms
allow_reject_ignore: 0.67 or 0.667 (kHz POT slip) scores 1 mark only
pitfalls: Forgetting to convert ms to s
Counting divisions for half a cycle

questions.context: Find wavelength of sound given its speed and the frequency found earlier.
allow_reject_ignore: If 667 Hz used λ = 0.495 m so allow 0.50 or 0.5 m

questions.context: Effect on trace when intensity falls to a quarter, oscilloscope settings unchanged.
questions.answer: Trace height smaller; I ∝ A², so amplitude halves (2 div / 20 mV).
marking_points: B1: amplitude/height of trace is smaller
B1: intensity ∝ amplitude² so amplitude halves (2 div or 20 mV)
allow_reject_ignore: The second point also scores the first

questions.context: State the principle of superposition.
questions.answer: Where waves meet, resultant displacement equals the sum of individual displacements.
marking_points: B1: resultant displacement = sum of the individual displacements (where waves meet)

questions.context: Meaning of coherent.
allow_reject_ignore: Not 'same phase difference' or 'zero phase difference'
pitfalls: Writing 'same phase difference' or 'in phase' instead of constant phase difference

questions.context: Path difference at the first maximum from the central maximum (microwaves, two slits).
pitfalls: Giving 2λ by counting A as first maximum

questions.context: Path difference at the second minimum point.
pitfalls: Giving λ/2 (that is the first minimum)

questions.context: Effect on maxima separation of increasing slit separation.
questions.answer: Separation of maxima decreases since x = λD/a with λ and D constant.
marking_points: M1: λ = ax/D quoted with D and λ constant (or x ∝ 1/a)
allow_reject_ignore: Allow other correct reasoning e.g. via path difference and angles

questions.context: Use W = VQ to express the volt in SI base units.
questions.answer: V = J/C = kg m² s^-2 /(A s) = kg m² A^-1 s^-3
marking_points: C1: J = N m = kg m s^-2 × m
M1: clear substitution V = kg m² s^-2 / (A s)

questions.context: Describe a safe experiment (with diagram) to find a wire's breaking stress and how to analyse data.
questions.answer: Clamp wire, add masses incrementally until break, measure diameter with micrometer, stress = F/A.
marking_points: L3 (5-6): clear procedure, measurements and analysis; well-developed, logically structured reasoning
L2 (3-4): some procedure, some measurements and some analysis; some structure
L1 (1-2): limited procedure and limited measurements or limited analysis; unstructured
Procedure: labelled diagram; increase load in increments until break; method of fixing wire and attaching load; safety screen/goggles; secure stand (G-clamp)
Measurements: load/mass; diameter with micrometer, averaged at several places; repeat experiment
Analysis: F = mg; A = πd²/4; breaking stress = maximum force / cross-sectional area
pitfalls: No analysis stated (caps at lower level)

questions.context: Sketch loading/unloading stress-strain graphs for glass and rubber.
questions.answer: Glass: straight line through origin (same for unloading); rubber: hysteresis loop starting and ending at origin.
marking_points: B1: glass - straight line from origin
B1: rubber - correct loading and unloading curves (loop) starting and ending at origin
allow_reject_ignore: Allow arrows or labels for rubber curves
pitfalls: Rubber loop not returning to origin

questions.context: Explain electroscope observations with light and UV as evidence for photoelectric effect and photons.
questions.answer: UV photons exceed work function, emit electrons so leaf falls; intensity only changes rate; visible photons below threshold regardless of intensity.
marking_points: L3 (5-6): clear explanation of observations AND clear evidence of particulate nature; well-developed, logical reasoning
L2 (3-4): clear explanation OR clear evidence, or limited explanation and limited evidence; some structure
L1 (1-2): limited explanation or limited evidence; unstructured

Observations: leaf falls as electrons (negative charge) emitted; intensity depends on distance; more photons per second when closer; higher UV photon rate → faster fall; UV discharge is immediate; light has no effect regardless of intensity; slow fall with light is natural leakage

Particle evidence: wave theory predicts light would eventually discharge; photon = packet of energy E = hf; one-to-one photon-electron interaction; UV photon energy > work function (f > threshold); light photon energy < work function; photon energy independent of intensity; energy conserved; Einstein's equation
pitfalls: Saying brighter light gives electrons more energy
Not explaining the role of distance/intensity

questions.context: Max KE in joules of photoelectrons given frequency and work function in eV.
pitfalls: Adding instead of subtracting work function

questions.context: Show speed of electrons accelerated from rest through 300 V.
pitfalls: Giving only 1.0 × 10^7 without more s.f. in a show-that

questions.context: de Broglie wavelength of the electrons.
pitfalls: Using electron charge instead of mass

questions.context: How the diffraction rings change when accelerating pd increases.
questions.answer: Electrons gain momentum so de Broglie wavelength falls; rings become smaller (less diffraction).
marking_points: B1: momentum/KE/speed increases or wavelength decreases
B1: ring radius decreases / pattern smaller (or rings brighter)
